WHAT SORT OF DAY DO YOU FANCY?

A little inspiration to get you going.

BUCKET & SPADE OPTIONAL

The classic seaside day

Start with a beach or promenade walk, stop for lunch and save the afternoon for a pier, a ride or a few games. Pick one resort and enjoy it properly.

Find a seaside escape →
RAIN WON’T SPOIL THIS ONE

The indoor adventure

Choose a museum, cinema or bowling session as your main event. Check the session times first, then find food nearby so the day keeps flowing even when the weather doesn’t.

Museums →Bowling →Cinema →
NO NEED TO RUSH HOME

The weekend wander

Choose a town, one thing you really want to do and somewhere to stay. Leave gaps for cafés, side streets and the places you spot along the way.

Make a short break of it →
PICK A PLACE. MAKE A DAY OF IT.

Where shall we go?

Skegness puts the beach, pier and fairground close together. Southport’s Marine Lake makes a good starting point for a waterfront wander. Great Yarmouth’s Golden Mile mixes beach time with attractions along the seafront. Choose the pace that suits your group, then open the town guide for the next stop.

THE BIT EVERYONE’S LOOKING FORWARD TO

Make room for a big adventure

A theme park can be the whole day; a castle or museum can be one stop in a bigger wander. Check ticket dates, age or height rules and access information before you book. Give your main attraction enough time and build the food stop around it.

Explore attractions →
LUNCH DESERVES A PLAN TOO

A good day needs a good food stop

Chips on the prom, a café break or a sit-down meal: choose somewhere that fits your route and the people coming with you. Look at the menu and service times before setting off, especially if you need a children’s menu or allergy information.

Find a food stop →
ONE MORE DAY? GO ON THEN.

Stay for the evening. Explore tomorrow.

Choose your base by what you want to do, then compare the full stay: room type, parking, breakfast and the cancellation terms. A central hotel and a quieter place outside town can give you very different weekends.

A LITTLE NOSTALGIA. A LOT OF FUN.

There’s always room for play

Seaside games, retro favourites and family entertainment are still part of the adventure. Family arcades and adult gaming centres are different places: check the venue type and age rules before taking children. Pick a play stop that fits the rest of your day.
